items.title: MOH to conduct special recruitment for 750 permanent medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from November 9 to 15. MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on December 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on October 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired. The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission’s SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.

items.title: Former Pahang water firm procurement manager begins three-year jail term after losing bribery appeal
items.summary: A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin ruled that Sani Khan Ali Khan had failed to show any error of law or material fact in the High Court decision that convicted him on all the charges. On January 26, the Kuantan High Court set aside a Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged him of all the charges. In today’s proceedings, Justice Noorin said the High Court’s intervention was justified and that it had made no material error in setting aside the Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged Sani Khan.

items.title: Fahmi: Malaysian films rake in RM129.9m as local animation pushes deeper into overseas markets
items.summary: Among the highest-grossing films were Tarung: Unforgiven (RM23.59 million), Chelot (RM19.12 million), Polong (RM15.05 million), Libang Libu (RM14.16 million) and Malaikat Malam (RM12.23 million). In animation, Fahmi said, Papa Zola The Movie earned RM63.84 million in Malaysia and more than RM69 million across Southeast Asia as of February 2026, highlighting the regional appeal of Malaysian productions. Under the 12th Malaysia Plan, the Creative Content Fund (DKK) supported 1,677 local creative projects, generating 32,795 employment opportunities.

items.title: Scam syndicates prepared fake passports, flight tickets to flee Malaysia
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The two foreign online scam syndicates crippled in Seri Kembangan and Jalan Kerinchi had prepared forged passports and flight tickets to flee the country if their activities were exposed to enforcement authorities. The syndicates were busted by the Immigration Department following two raids yesterday and this morning. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said investigators discovered three passport booklets bearing the names of Japan, South Korea and the United States, raising suspicions that syndicate members had made advance preparations to flee.

items.title: Sanusi: Singapore has 'Singlish', I am from Sik... we have 'Siklish'
items.summary: He said communication skills should not be assessed solely based on grammatical accuracy, but rather on how effectively a message is conveyed to the audience. he said after a lecture programme on "The Greater Kedah". He said this in response to social media users' criticism of his use of English when he raised the issue of rare earth elements (REE) at the SG4 forum.

items.title: HeiTech Padu clarifies Zetrix AI teaming agreement, both parties agreed not to extend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HeiTech Padu Bhd today clarified that the Teaming Agreement it entered into with Zetrix AI Bhd on April 16, 2024, was an interim collaboration to explore potential opportunities to provide information technology services in Malaysia. "Accordingly, there is no ongoing collaboration between HeiTech Padu and Zetrix in relation to the National Integrated Immigration System (NIISe) project pursuant to the Teaming Agreement. On the Supplemental Agreement signed with Zetrix on Aug 4, 2025, HeiTech Padu said it was intended to record both parties' understanding of their respective obligations and roles under the original Teaming Agreement.

items.title: Two scam syndicates collect RM6mil in 2 months, 64 arrested
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Two online scam syndicates believed to have raked in RM6 million in just two months have been crippled following raids on luxury condominiums and bungalows in the Klang Valley, with 64 foreigners arrested. The syndicates, which operated from four luxury condominium units in Jalan Kerinchi, Kuala Lumpur, and two bungalows in The Mines, Seri Kembangan, were generating between RM100,000 and RM150,000 daily by targeting victims through fraudulent investment schemes and offers of non-existent services. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the two-day operation on Oct 28 and 29 resulted in the arrest of 44 Chinese nationals, 19 Vietnamese nationals and one Myanmar national.

items.title: Pahang's RM850mil Chereh Dam solar project to create 1,500 jobs
items.summary: KUANTAN: A RM850 million floating solar photovoltaic (PV) project at Chereh Dam in Pahang is expected to create about 1,500 jobs and generate clean electricity equivalent to the annual consumption of 100,000 households. Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah said the project, a collaboration between Citaglobal Bhd, Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC (Masdar) and Tiza Global Sdn Bhd, marked a major step towards expanding the state's use of renewable energy. Meanwhile, Citaglobal New Energy Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Chairil Nazri Ahmad said floating solar technology could improve electricity generation efficiency because panels installed over water generally operate at lower temperatures than those mounted on land.

items.title: S P Setia offers homebuyers cash rewards until December
items.summary: Running from Oct 1 to Dec 31, the promotion also features events at participating sales galleries across the Klang Valley, Penang and Johor, giving prospective buyers opportunities to explore the developer's properties. SALES GALLERY EVENTS As part of HomeFest 2026, S P Setia is hosting events at participating sales galleries across the Klang Valley, Penang and Johor. The scheduled events include: Klang Valley - Oct 31 to Nov 1: Setia Alamsari Welcome Centre, Kajang - Nov 21: Setia Alamsari Welcome Centre, Kajang - Nov 21 to 22: Bandar Setia Alam Sales Gallery, Setia Alam - Nov 21 to 22: Temasya Glenmarie Welcome Centre, Shah Alam - Nov 28 to 29: LakePoint Gallerie, Alam Impian, Shah Alam - Dec 5: Setia Warisan Tropika Sales Gallery, Sepang - Dec 12: Setia International Centre, KL Eco City, Bangsar Penang - Nov 28: Setia Sales Suites, George Town - Dec 5: Setia Fontaines, Kepala Batas Johor - Nov 14: Taman Rinting Sales Gallery, Masai - Nov 21: Setia Eco Gardens Sales Gallery, Gelang Patah The events give prospective buyers an opportunity to learn more about participating developments and explore available property options.

items.title: Ahmad Shahazan Yacob elected MIA's new president, former Bursa chief Umar Swift is VP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Institute of Accountants (MIA) has elected Ahmad Syahazan Yaacob as its new president and Datuk Muhamad Umar Swift as vice-president effective today. Ahmad succeeds Datuk Saniza Said, whose tenure as president ended on Sept 26, 2026. "MIA congratulates Ahmad and Umar on their election as president and vice president respectively.

items.title: MACC orders ex-Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman, brother to declare assets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has ordered former Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin and his elder brother, Datuk Mubarak Hussain Akhtar Husin, to declare their assets. Both men were issued asset declaration notices on Oct 20, with Nazir understood to have received his at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed that both men had received and accepted the notices issued under Section 36 of the MACC Act.

items.title: Sanusi: Pas to contest two seats in Melaka election
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Pas will field candidates in two seats in the upcoming Melaka election, with another five seats being contested by other Perikatan Nasional component parties. "Pas has two seats. I can only confirm Pas (has two seats).

items.title: CSA unrelated to Bersatu-PH cooperation in Melaka, says Muhyiddin
items.summary: Asked by reporters whether Bersatu would form an electoral pact with PH in Melaka, he said: "That's another question. He was speaking after signing the agreement at Parliament here with several other Bersatu members of Parliament, including Datuk Seri Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai). Deputy Prime Ministers Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, as well as Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, were also present.

items.title: Menara Tun Perak, formerly Menara Maybank, on offer for full or partial sale
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Menara Tun Perak, the iconic Kuala Lumpur skyscraper formerly known as Menara Maybank, has reportedly been put up for sale after serving as the banking giant’s headquarters for nearly four decades. On July 28, Maybank announced that its new headquarters would be renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank, while its former headquarters would take the name Menara Tun Perak. Knight Frank Malaysia head of capital markets James Buckley said properties of such prominence in Kuala Lumpur's historic commercial district were seldom offered to investors.

items.title: Indonesian police probe 97 corporations over forest fires, 20 named as suspects
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian police are investigating 97 corporations, including 22 foreign-linked companies, over forest and land fire cases across the country, with 20 companies already named as suspects. National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) chief Comm Gen Asep Safrudin said 16 of the 20 corporate suspects were domestically invested companies, while the remaining four were foreign-invested. He said police had so far received 104 reports involving corporations, covering 29,168.78 hectares of burned land, including 33 reports in West Kalimantan, 20 in South Sumatra, 14 in Central Kalimantan, 13 in South Kalimantan, and seven in East Kalimantan.

items.title: 5 hours to travel 6km amid Bangsar traffic chaos
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists were caught in severe traffic congestion for hours in Lembah Pantai, Bangsar and Kampung Kerinchi yesterday following heavy rain and fallen trees. Social media posts showed motorists enduring nearly five hours of slow-moving traffic while travelling to pick up their children from school, despite their homes being just a few kilometres away. Threads user @lyslysa said she spent nearly five hours travelling from Bangsar South or Kampung Kerinchi to SK Bangsar and back to Pantai Hillpark.

items.title: Violent threats from smugglers a part of life for border enforcement personnel
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Violent threats from smugglers are part of life for border enforcement personnel. Smugglers they encounter shout threats at them and occasionally fire shots at them using firearms and air guns. Irwandi said smuggling activities along the border involved various contraband, including drugs, firearms and rice.

items.title: Community-led innovation for future cities
items.summary: LETTER: Malaysia has made remarkable progress in expanding access to housing, most recently pushing past national targets by delivering more than 511,000 affordable housing units under the Twelfth Malaysia Plan. Large-scale public housing programmes, urban upgrading efforts and investments in infrastructure have helped improve living conditions for many communities. As climate change intensifies, the need for resilient housing, risk-informed planning and safer urban development becomes increasingly important.

items.title: Muhyiddin: CSA has nothing to do with possible Bersatu-PH pact for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed with the federal government today has nothing to do with a possible electoral pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported. Muhyiddin also said the CSA was separate from a similar agreement being sought between Bersatu and the PH-led Selangor government, the report said. According to FMT, the CSA involved six Bersatu MPs and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.

items.title: MCA gets Bandar Hilir as third seat to contest in Melaka, ending BN seat dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will contest Bandar Hilir as its third seat in the Melaka election, ending a seat allocation dispute within Barisan Nasional. Party president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the agreement followed discussions between BN and Perikatan Nasional, whose leaders agreed to let MCA contest the seat. Wee said PN would announce candidates for six seats.

items.title: Muhyiddin hopes confidence and supply agreement will last until Parliament is dissolved
items.summary: Those spotted at the signing included Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman. Representing the government were deputy prime ministers Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, as well as Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. Muhyiddin said the agreement followed the format of the one signed when Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was prime minister and Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was opposition leader.

items.title: Kedah police arrest man over viral video of reckless driving in ‘Bomba’ MPV
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 29 — Police have arrested a 35-year-old man over a viral video showing him allegedly driving recklessly in a red multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) bearing the word ‘Bomba’. Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said investigations found that the man had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder nine years ago but was believed to have discontinued treatment about two years ago. Hanyan said the man owned the MPV, held a valid driving licence and had no previous criminal record.

items.title: Govt deputy ministers welcome Bersatu CSA, say pact shows Madani respects all elected reps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Madani government respects all elected representatives regardless of their party’s size or political strength, Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said today, following Bersatu’s signing of a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the government. The Segamat MP said that despite having a two-thirds majority in Parliament, the government should still engage with the opposition rather than assume it can act unilaterally. “Unlike some coalitions that prioritise political grandstanding over genuine democratic bargaining, the Madani government has demonstrated that negotiations can be conducted with dignity, mutual respect and a firm commitment to democratic principles,” he said.

items.title: Transport minister takes first AirBorneo flight, stresses need for reliable air links to remote communities
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 29 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke took his first flight with AirBorneo on a trip from Miri to Limbang, highlighting the importance of rural air connectivity for communities in Sarawak and Sabah. “Reliable air connectivity is an absolute lifeline for communities in the interior of Sarawak and Sabah. Beyond its Rural Air Services, AirBorneo also operates scheduled domestic and international passenger flights.

items.title: Amir Hamzah: Malaysia confident of exceeding 5pc GDP growth in 2026 as strong economy benefits the people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The government is confident that economic growth will exceed 5.0 per cent this year, marking the third consecutive year of growth above 5.0 per cent under the Madani Government, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. “Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026. Amir Hamzah said growth in 2027 is projected to be between 4.2 and 5.2 per cent.

items.title: 6 Bersatu MPs, Syed Saddiq sign deal to back Anwar until term ends
items.summary: They also want to receive the same constituency development allocations as government MPs. In return, the seven opposition MPs will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration until the end of the parliamentary term, including the 2027 Budget. Eight independent MPs also support the government, including six former Bersatu representatives.

items.title: MCMC reviewing need for further regulations on online games, including Roblox, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is reviewing the need for further regulatory measures on online gaming platforms, including Roblox, to enhance child protection against digital safety risks. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, together with the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF), is currently studying online gaming trends and associated risks, including user-to-user interactions, in-game content, and protective safeguards implemented by platform providers. Fahmi said the government is also prioritising parental education and awareness, particularly on activating parental control functions on personal devices and online services.

items.title: Hong Kong leader apologises for deadly Tai Po fire, pledges reforms
items.summary: HONG KONG: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologised on Thursday for the deadly blaze that killed 168 people in the city last November, promising swift but extensive reforms to its building industry and regulatory system. Lee was speaking shortly before he released a more than 1,000-page report by the judge-led panel that detailed wide-ranging governance and supervisory failings in Hong Kong's building-renovation system. Lee also announced the resignation of Hong Kong's Housing Secretary Winnie Ho, echoing the report by saying that four government bodies bore partial responsibility for a blaze that the report said was most likely started by a "glowing source...likely a cigarette."

items.title: Never exploit royal ties and influence for profit - Sultan Nazrin
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR: The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, has warned members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court against misusing the Ruler's name, royal influence and their titles for personal gain. His Royal Highness cautioned against exploiting such privileges for financial profit or business opportunities. Sultan Nazrin also urged members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court to remain vigilant and exercise sound judgement in communications, particularly when using social media channels and platforms.

items.title: Syed Saddiq: CSA must ensure fair funding, curb PM's powers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) must deliver genuine reforms before the next general election. He said the reforms would curb the prime minister's powers and ensure fair constituency funding, with legislation needed to bind future administrations. A live video on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's Facebook page showed Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Anwar's senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, at the signing.

items.title: High Court upholds 17-year jail sentence for man in gang rape case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has upheld a 17-year jail sentence imposed on a man who took turns with two others to rape their friend's 26-year-old sister-in-law in 2023. Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin dismissed 31-year-old Nik Khaira Hafizi Mat Zaid's appeal against the sentence imposed by the Sessions Court on June 16, 2024. Nik Khaira and two others took turns to rape the victim while the fourth man helped restrain her and watched the assault.

items.title: Malay reserve land accounts for 91.58pc of titled land in Kelantan, says MB
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — Malay Reserve Land in Kelantan covers 526,083.08 hectares as of June this year, accounting for 91.58 per cent of the total 574,427.61 hectares of titled land recorded in the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud. “For the other districts, Kota Bharu recorded 40,510.49 hectares (99.97 per cent), Pasir Mas 56,656.79 hectares (99.98 per cent), Kuala Krai 53,473.85 hectares (68.73 per cent) and Tumpat 21,607.96 hectares (99.99 per cent). “Bachok recorded 26,541.25 hectares (99.98 per cent), Tanah Merah 56,246.13 hectares (99.98 per cent), Pasir Puteh 43,377.81 hectares (99.99 per cent), Machang 28,376.83 hectares (96.18 per cent), Jeli 37,240.60 hectares (99.93 per cent) and Lojing 39,315.82 hectares (98.99 per cent),” he said in reply to a question from Datuk Mohd Shabuddin Hashim (BN-Galas).

items.title: Malaysia’s new vehicle brings geospatial tools together for faster disaster response
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — A Defence Geospatial Information Rapid Team (DGIRT) vehicle has been introduced as a pilot project to accelerate the delivery of geospatial information in the field, supporting defence, security and disaster management operations. Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the vehicle integrates specialised geospatial equipment to enable faster and more accurate field data collection. He was speaking at a press conference after launching Defence Geospatial Day 2026 (DG’26), themed “Advancing Defence and Security Through Geospatial Capabilities”, at Wisma Perwira today.

items.title: Malaysian family robbed of 11 bags during Italy trip
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian family travelling in Italy was left distressed after 11 pieces of luggage were allegedly stolen from their car while they stopped for a meal in Pisa. One commenter advised travellers to head directly from their hotels or accommodation to the airport without making unnecessary stops. Another user, farhayayakob, warned travellers against using expensive luggage brands and leaving their bags in a car in a public area.

items.title: Bersatu signs confidence and supply pact with Madani govt, says MPs to get same allocations as govt backbenchers
items.summary: According to the English daily, Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the agreement would allow the party’s MPs to receive the same constituency development allocations as government backbenchers. “I signed on behalf of Bersatu and there are also the other six who previously showed support to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Muhyiddin said the agreement followed a similar arrangement during the administration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, when Anwar was the opposition leader.

items.title: Skip toll payments and risk being tracked under new MLFF system, says works minister
items.summary: PORT KLANG, Oct 29 — The full implementation of the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection system is expected to help address the issue of toll evasion, including by identifying motorists who commit such offences. Minister of Works Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the Ministry of Works (KKR), through the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), continuously monitors the efficiency and effectiveness of toll systems nationwide which are developed by highway concession companies. “Therefore, the implementation of the Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) system at toll plaza lanes will also assist in obtaining information regarding individuals who commit toll evasion.

items.title: Man found dead in storeroom
items.summary: LAWAS: A 35-year-old man was found lying dead in a storeroom at a government agency here yesterday. Lawas district police chief Deputy Superintendent Liong Tindan said the man was pronounced dead by medical personnel who examined him. "Initial investigations at the scene found no elements of crime involving the victim," he said.

items.title: Philippine minister says Asean does not share China's view on defence forum
items.summary: CEBU: The Philippine defence minister said on Thursday that Asean countries do not share the view of China's defence ministry on the its participation in a regional defence forum, adding that no country has the right to characterise Asean processes. How Asean countries are heard is for Asean to determine, and the important fact is China was able to articulate their position, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said, Beijing, however, accused Manila of "erecting multiple obstacles" for its attendance at an Asean meeting in the Philippines this week, where China will be represented by an embassy attache. "The Philippine side has allowed certain politicians to use public office for private ends and erected multiple obstacles to obstruct China's participation in the Asean Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus," a spokesperson for the Chinese defence ministry told a news conference.

items.title: Sabah targets RM100b GDP by 2030 through investment, industrial growth, says CM
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — Sabah is pursuing various initiatives to achieve a gross domestic product (GDP) target of RM100 billion by 2030 under its Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development agenda, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the state government was focusing on implementing industrial development plans, attracting investments and providing essential infrastructure, including a stable, reliable and affordable energy supply. Hajiji said Sabah’s gas supply had the potential to increase from approximately 700 million standard cubic feet per day to 1,350 million standard cubic feet per day by 2030, based on the Long-Term Gas Supply and Transmission Plan presented to the state government last September.

items.title: Hajiji: Sabah allocates RM98.06m to empower youth, boost role in policymaking
items.summary: TUARAN, Oct 29 — The Sabah government is strengthening youth participation in policymaking through initiatives such as the Chief Minister’s Young Thinkers (Pemikir Muda) initiative and the Sabah Youth Assembly, providing platforms for young people to contribute ideas on the state’s development. “Youth are a vital asset in determining the direction and future of Sabah. Therefore, the Chief Minister’s Young Thinkers initiative provides a space for Sabah’s youth to be directly involved in the formulation of state development policies.

items.title: Kelantan tables RM1.38b Budget 2027 with RM4.31m operating deficit
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — The Kelantan state government today tabled a RM1.383 billion Budget 2027, comprising RM1.087 billion in operating expenditure and RM296 million for development. He said state revenue for 2027 was projected at RM1.082 billion, comprising RM238.8 million in tax revenue, RM314.5 million in non-tax revenue, and RM529.29 million in non-revenue receipts. “Land-related revenue is projected at RM373.57 million, forestry revenue at RM70.4 million and mining revenue at RM48.41 million.

items.title: South China Sea territorial contest a test of Asean’s unity and credibility, says Mohamed Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Asean member states should not allow overlapping maritime claims in the South China Sea to fracture the peace and solidarity in the region, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. Speaking at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM), Mohamed Khaled said the Asean solidarity is one of the bloc’s greatest strengths that must be preserved. Asean Defence Ministers’ pose for the symbolic Asean handshake at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting in Cebu, the Philippines.

items.title: Strengthening national resilience through environmental security
items.summary: MALAYSIA'S environmental approach rests on the National Policy on the Environment (DASN), which promotes sustainable resource use and the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (EQA), providing a legal basis for pollution control. Malaysia also participates in the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP), recognising that some environmental risks cannot be managed within national borders alone. Environmental monitoring also offers an opportunity to act earlier.

items.title: Hello Kitty firm scraps Japan TV tie-up after 'anti-China' backlash
items.summary: BEIJING: Sanrio, the Japanese company that owns the popular Hello Kitty character, apologised Thursday over its tie-up with a TV spy drama criticised as anti-China, cancelling a merchandise collaboration with the show. "We have recently received feedback from various quarters regarding the collaborative merchandise with the Japanese television drama VIVANT," Sanrio's Chinese unit said on social media platform Weibo. The project "contains expressions that are inconsistent with the Sanrio Group's corporate philosophy", it said.

items.title: Penang awaits full report on fatal Paya Terubong landslide as probe continues
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Oct 29 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has submitted a draft technical report on the recent landslide at Taman Seri Permai, Paya Terubong, to the state government, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the report was still being followed up and reviewed before a detailed report on the incident could be finalised. Chow said matters related to technical planning would be handled by state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye, while the welfare of affected residents would be coordinated by state Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai, who is also the Paya Terubong assemblyman.

items.title: Parkland wins approval for Main Market listing, to issue 621.54mil new shares
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Property developer Parkland Bhd has received approval from the Securities Commission (SC) for its initial public offering (IPO) and proposed listing on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia. The IPO will comprise 621.54 million shares, representing 26.3 per cent of the group's enlarged issued share capital of 2.36 billion shares upon listing. It will comprise a public issue of 468.14 million new shares and an offer for sale of 153.40 million existing shares.

items.title: KTMB offers record 1.57 million ETS, ERT seats for January to March 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is offering a record 1,573,872 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Ekspres Rakyat Timuran (ERT) from January to March 2027, a 39 per cent increase over the same period this year. In a statement today, KTMB said ticket sales for both services will open in stages from November 2, allowing the public to plan travel ahead of school holidays, public holidays and festive seasons. With demand rising, KTMB will increase ETS service frequency in 2027 from 44 scheduled services a day in 2026 to 50 services a day from Monday to Thursday and 58 services a day from Friday to Sunday, an increase of between six and 14 services a day.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin tells Dewan Negara Perak members, palace dignitaries not to exploit royal ties for profit
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 29 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, has warned members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court against misusing the Ruler’s name, royal influence and their titles for personal gain, financial profit or business opportunities. Sultan Nazrin also urged members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court to remain vigilant and exercise sound judgement in communications, particularly when using social media channels and platforms. Sultan Nazrin said members of Dewan Negara Perak and royal dignitaries must understand the role of the monarchy within the framework of a constitutional monarchy.

items.title: Thailand targets US$1bil in assets as alleged scam suspects flee
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thai authorities have vowed to seize more than US$1 billion in assets from a group accused of laundering proceeds from Southeast Asia-based scam syndicates. A criminal court issued arrest warrants Tuesday for the alleged ring leader, South African Ben Smith, his Thai wife Cattaliya Beevor, Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and four others, police said. Smith, Cattaliya, Yim Leak and three others have fled Thailand, the country's Securities and Exchange Commission said in a statement.

items.title: Court of Appeal allows lawyer Rosli Dahlan to challenge police, prosecution seizure of four ASNB accounts
items.summary: A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously allowed Rosli’s appeal to overturn a High Court decision that had dismissed his leave application. Delivering the court’s decision, Justice Choo held that the High Court had erred in disallowing Rosli’s application for leave to initiate the judicial review. The learned High Court judge therefore erred in refusing leave for this preliminary stage,” Justice Choo said.

items.title: Spain declares three days of mourning after train crash kills 68, injures over 100
items.summary: URDA: Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after its second high-speed rail collision this year killed 68 people and injured scores, with relatives desperately seeking news about their loved ones. One of Europe's deadliest train disasters this century has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain's rail network after the transport minister reported an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" that led to the crash. Emergency services combed through the wreckage at night to find further victims on the key line linking Madrid with the southern city of Seville, hoisting pieces of mangled metal with cranes, AFP reporters saw.

items.title: Sabah’s 40pc revenue rights appeal: Court of Appeal to decide on Nov 12
items.summary: The three-judge panel comprising Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Datuk Amarjeet Singh Serjit Singh fixed the date for e-Review case management after hearing submissions from the federal government, the Sabah Law Society (SLS) and the Sabah government today. The federal government is challenging parts of the Kota Kinabalu High Court ruling, including findings that both the federal and Sabah governments had abused their powers and breached their constitutional responsibilities. However, SLS said the federal government’s notice of appeal did not challenge the 40 per cent constitutional formula or the need for a review under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: US fires top army general in latest ouster: Media
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States has fired its top military planner, The Atlantic reported Wednesday, in a surprise shake-up as President Donald Trump appears to be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed this week from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the magazine reported, citing unidentified defence department officials. Sylvia's ouster would be the latest in a series of high-profile departures from the military since Trump returned to power a year ago.

items.title: IWK suspects dislocated joint on 30-year-old pipe caused Bayan Baru sinkhole, repairs due Nov 7
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 29 — Indah Water Konsortium Sdn Bhd (IWK) has launched an immediate investigation into a sinkhole incident along Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir in Bayan Baru here, which is suspected to have been caused by a dislocated sewer pipe joint. In a statement today, IWK said its site investigation began immediately after it received public complaints about the incident, and emergency repair works to restore the affected sewerage infrastructure have also been initiated, with completion targeted for November 7, 2026, weather permitting. IWK said this was the first reported incident of its kind in the area, with no previous complaints related to sewer defects recorded.

items.title: Malaysia stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia, condemns Houthi attacks, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Malaysia has expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid its current security challenges and affirmed its readiness to assist within its capabilities. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said he conveyed the message during a telephone conversation with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, yesterday. “Malaysia stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid its current security challenges and remains ready to assist within our capabilities.

items.title: Malaysians arrested on drug charges in 40 countries, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Forty countries have recorded the arrest of Malaysian citizens in drug-related cases, with intensified enforcement in those countries among the factors driving greater attention to such offences, said Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni. He said Malaysia is working to clarify the situation with those countries, given its perceived high numbers in drug cases, which in turn have prompted tighter enforcement abroad. He also noted that cross-border drug smuggling methods are becoming more sophisticated, making the activity harder to curb and requiring close cooperation between enforcement agencies and countries.

items.title: Armizan: Domestic Trade Ministry weighs Nibong Tebal petrol station licence suspension after RM270,000 subsidy misuse detected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) will suspend or revoke a petrol station’s Control of Supplies Act (CSA) licence in Nibong Tebal, Penang if it is found misusing the BUDI Madani petrol subsidy. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the government could take such action under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 if the petrol station breaches licensing conditions, including manipulating transaction records or misappropriating government subsidies. On Tuesday, the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said it blocked a petrol station in Sungai Buaya, Nibong Tebal, from selling subsidised RON95 petrol and diesel under BUDI Madani after detecting suspicious subsidy misuse transactions.

items.title: Report: Bersatu to sign confidence and supply agreement with Madani govt this evening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) will sign a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the Madani government this evening, Sinar Harian reported. An online news portal reported that the signing would take place at the office of Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Sinar Harian added. According to the report, the agreement covers all 19 MPs who remain with Bersatu and is meant to guarantee support for Budget 2027 should Barisan Nasional (BN) withdraw its backing.

items.title: Melaka polls: PKR adds Ayer Limau, to contest 10 seats, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has added one more state seat to its list for the upcoming Melaka state election, bringing its total to 10 seats up from the nine previously announced. PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the additional seat is the Ayer Limau constituency, which will be contested by the party’s candidate, Major (Rtd) Jaimi Dimon. When we announced our candidates previously, it was for nine seats; today, we have added another, bringing the total number of seats to be contested by PKR to 10.

items.title: Johor DoE probes white effluent in Sungai Kim Kim, checks CCTV after pollution fears resurface
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Oct 29 — The Department of Environment (DoE) is investigating Sungai Kim Kim here after receiving reports of a white cloudy effluent, triggering fears that pollution has returned. The effluent, spotted near the bypass road between Taman Pasir Putih and Kota Masai here, is suspected of causing a foul odour reported since yesterday that has affected various areas around Johor Bahru and Pasir Gudang. White cloudy effluent seen in Sungai Kim Kim near the Taman Pasir Putih–Kota Masai bypass road in Pasir Gudang on October 29, 2026, raising fears of renewed pollution.
